_note: Original advanced concept questions for graphs.

questions.title: Nodes and edges
questions.code:
Graph:
A -- B
A -- C

A connection is an edge.
questions.prompt: In a graph, what does an edge represent?
choices: The last item in a stack
questions.explanation: Edges describe which nodes are connected. Traversal uses those connections to decide which neighbors can be visited next from the current node.

questions.title: Adjacency list
questions.prompt: What does an adjacency list store for each node?
questions.explanation: An adjacency list stores the neighbors for each node. Traversal reads that list to decide which nodes can be reached next.

questions.title: Visited set
questions.prompt: Why does graph traversal need a visited set?
choices: To avoid visiting the same node again
questions.explanation: Graphs can contain cycles, so visited prevents repeated work and infinite loops.

questions.title: BFS tool
questions.code:
BFS queue:
front [A] back

After visiting A:
front [B, C] back
questions.prompt: Which structure does breadth-first search usually use?
questions.explanation: BFS uses a queue because the oldest discovered node should be processed next. That is what makes BFS move level by level.

questions.title: DFS behavior
questions.code:
DFS path:
A -> B -> D

Go deep before backing up.
choices: Follow one path deeply before backing up
Visit every level before going deeper
questions.explanation: DFS follows one branch as far as it can before backing up. A stack or recursion keeps track of the path that still needs to finish.

questions.title: Cycle risk
questions.code:
A connects to B
B connects to A
No visited set is used
choices: The traversal can repeat A and B forever.
questions.explanation: A and B lead back to each other, so traversal needs visited to stop repeating them.

questions.title: Graph traversal setup
questions.prompt: Arrange the safe graph traversal steps.
lines: Add the start node to the work list.
While work remains, remove one node.
Visit unvisited neighbors and mark them visited.
questions.explanation: Traversal needs a start, a work list, and visited checks before adding neighbors repeatedly.

questions.title: Disconnected graph
questions.code:
Component 1: A -- B

Component 2: C -- D

Start at A only.
questions.prompt: Why might one traversal from a single start node miss part of a graph?
choices: The graph has too many strings.
The start node is always last.
questions.explanation: If some nodes are not connected to the start, they require another traversal start.
